questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Gibe / Jibe — Which meaning fits “Gibe”?

options.A: A baby's cot with barred sides; (informal) to copy dishonestly
options.B: Everyone or everything in one group or at the same time
options.C: To be in agreement or accord with (informal); to shift a sail
options.D: An insulting or mocking remark; to taunt

questions.explanation:
Gibe: An insulting or mocking remark; to taunt. Sentence: "He ignored the gibes of his classmates who laughed at his old shoes."
Jibe: (Sailing) to shift a sail across the boat; (informal) to agree or be consistent with. Sentence: "His story did not jibe with the evidence, so the police doubted him; the sailor shouted a warning as the boat jibed."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Epigram / Epigraph — Which meaning fits “Epigram”?

options.A: A large crowd of people, often disorderly or threatening
options.B: A short, witty saying expressing a clever idea
options.C: A quotation placed at the start of a book or chapter
options.D: Partly decayed plant matter from bogs, dried and used as fuel or compost

questions.explanation:
Epigram: A short, witty saying expressing a clever idea. Sentence: "Oscar Wilde's epigram 'I can resist everything except temptation' still makes readers smile."
Epigraph: A short quotation at the start of a book or chapter; an inscription on a building or statue. Sentence: "The novel opens with an epigraph from Iqbal that sets the theme of the whole story."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Brawl / Bawl — Which meaning fits “Brawl”?

options.A: A noisy, rough fight among people
options.B: Showing cruel disregard for others' feelings; insensitive
options.D: To cook food slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot

questions.explanation:
Brawl: A noisy, rough fight among people. Sentence: "A brawl broke out between rival fans after the match, and chairs were thrown."
Bawl: To cry or shout loudly and noisily. Sentence: "The lost child began to bawl until his mother ran back to pick him up."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Crib / Crypt — Which meaning fits “Crib”?

options.A: A story or deed of adventure, especially a heroic exploit (also 'geste')
options.B: An underground chamber beneath a church
options.C: A public uproar or controversy; a sudden craze (British spelling)
options.D: A baby's cot with barred sides; (informal) to copy dishonestly

questions.explanation:
Crib: A baby's cot with barred sides; (informal) to copy dishonestly. Sentence: "The baby slept peacefully in her crib; the student was caught trying to crib answers from his neighbour."
Crypt: An underground room or vault beneath a church, used for burial. Sentence: "The saint's tomb lies in the crypt beneath the cathedral floor."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Barmy / Balmy — Which meaning fits “Barmy”?

options.C: To scatter or plant seeds; (noun) a female pig
options.D: (British, Liverpool/Merseyside slang) a foolish or stupid person

questions.explanation:
Barmy: Mad, crazy, foolish (British informal). Sentence: "Swimming in the river in January is a barmy idea; you'll freeze."
Balmy: Pleasantly warm and mild (of weather or air). Sentence: "We sat on the lawn on a balmy spring evening with a gentle breeze blowing."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Peat / Petite — Which meaning fits “Peat”?

options.A: To cry or shout loudly and noisily
options.C: Partly decayed plant matter from bogs, dried and used as fuel or compost
options.D: A small open boat, often carried by a larger ship or used for leisure

questions.explanation:
Peat: Partly decayed plant matter from bogs, dried and used as fuel or compost. Sentence: "In the Irish countryside, families once burned peat cut from the bog to heat their homes."
Petite: Small and slim (usually of a woman); small-sized clothing. Sentence: "Being petite, she had to shorten the sleeves of every coat she bought."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Monogamous / Monogenous — Which meaning fits “Monogamous”?

options.A: Arising from a single origin or reproducing asexually
options.B: To disturb or unsettle someone's composure
options.C: Having only one spouse or mate at a time

questions.explanation:
Monogamous: Having only one spouse or mate at a time. Sentence: "Swans are monogamous birds that stay with one partner for life."
Monogenous: Having a single origin; (biology) produced asexually from one parent. Sentence: "Some scholars hold a monogenous view that all human languages descended from one ancestral tongue; bacteria show monogenous reproduction by simple division."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2021 · Pair: Postilion / Posterior — Which meaning fits “Postilion”?

options.A: A short quotation at the start of a book or chapter; an inscription on a building or statue
options.B: Situated behind or at the rear; later in time
options.C: A person who rides the leading near-side horse of a team drawing a carriage
options.D: A sledge drawn by horses or reindeer, used for travel on snow

questions.explanation:
Postilion: A person who rides the leading near-side horse of a team drawing a carriage. Sentence: "Before motor cars, a postilion rode one of the front horses to guide the carriage."
Posterior: Further back in position or later in time; (informal) the buttocks. Sentence: "The posterior part of the brain controls vision, while the front handles planning."
Source: CSS 2021 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).
